# FlexVara

> A single-page buyer's guide to FlexVara, the NUVICA Wellness joint wellness capsule, sold as 60 capsules per bottle and taken two capsules daily. Written for readers in the United States at https://us-flexvara.vercel.app/. Orders complete on the official checkout with ClickBank as retailer of record. Last reviewed 16 November 2026.

FlexVara is built on NEM eggshell membrane rather than the glucosamine and chondroitin that dominate the joint-supplement shelf. A two-capsule serving supplies NEM eggshell membrane 500 mg, boswellia extract 150 mg, calcium 75 mg at 6% of the Daily Value, turmeric root extract 50 mg standardised to 95% curcuminoids, ginger root extract 20 mg, hydrolyzed collagen 5 mg and black pepper fruit extract 5 mg, for 805 mg of active material. Every amount is published individually and nothing is grouped into a blend total. Carrier ingredients are microcrystalline cellulose, hypromellose for the capsule shell, magnesium stearate and silicon dioxide. The label carries a CONTAINS EGG allergen declaration because the lead ingredient is derived from hen eggshells; the product is otherwise stated to be free of dairy, soy and gluten, and described as non-GMO. One bottle lasts 30 days, and the maker recommends at least three to six months of use. Packages cost $69, $59 and $49 per bottle for two, three and six bottles, with free US shipping and the newsletter bonus on the three and six bottle packages. Every package carries a 90-day money-back guarantee. One payment, no subscription. Sold to adults 18 and over.

## Sources cited on this page

- [NIAMS: osteoarthritis research and resources](https://www.niams.nih.gov/health-topics/osteoarthritis/more-info): the US institute covering arthritis and musculoskeletal conditions, with plain-language resources.
- [MedlinePlus: osteoarthritis](https://medlineplus.gov/osteoarthritis.html): consumer background on joint conditions and what to raise with a clinician.
- [NIH Office of Dietary Supplements: calcium](https://ods.od.nih.gov/factsheets/Calcium/): recommended intakes and upper limits, relevant to the 75 mg in each serving.
- [NIH Office of Dietary Supplements: what you need to know](https://ods.od.nih.gov/factsheets/WYNTK-Consumer/): a plain-language primer on dietary supplements and how they are regulated.
- [NIH LiverTox: turmeric](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK548561/): background on turmeric, including rare liver-injury reports that mostly involve high-dose curcumin products.
- [FDA: dietary supplements](https://www.fda.gov/food/dietary-supplements): supplements sit under food law rather than medicines law in the United States.
- [FTC: health claims](https://www.ftc.gov/business-guidance/advertising-marketing/health-claims): the advertising rules a supplement health claim has to meet.
